title: Temporal-correlation-driven alert deduplication and autoremediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy pages and improve on-call efficiency by grouping temporally-related signals, suppressing duplicates, and enabling safe automated remediation for well-understood failure classes. This ticket implements a temporal-correlation engine and orchestration hooks so that multi-region failovers, circuit breaker tripping, and load-shedding events do not generate redundant pager noise while preserving SLO awareness and human-in-the-loop escalation for high-risk actions.

Background: We currently observe bursty alert storms when KV cache pressure or kernel OOMs surface across many nodes. These storms trigger per-node alerts that multiply into pages and hamstring on-call triage. Past mitigations (static dedupe windows, simple rate limits) cut noise but either hide actionable degradation or delay response. We need a smarter grouping model that uses timing, signal type, topology (region/zone/service), and SLO impact to decide: group+suppress, sample+notify, or auto-remediate.

Scope:
- Implement temporal-correlation service that consumes alert stream (Alertmanager events / webhook) and emits grouped incidents with a confidence score.
- Add policies for grouping thresholds per signal class (e.g., KV-miss spikes, request error ratios, 5xx tail latency).
- Integrate with runbook-orchestration: attach a canonical runbook to grouped incidents and optionally run safe remediation playbooks (restart pod on non-critical pool, drain & reinstate node, increase circulation of dedicated capacity) under strict guardrails.
- Provide exponential backoff sampling for low-confidence repeats so SREs still receive visibility without a full-page explosion.
- Add telemetry: pages/week, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to remediation (MTTR), grouping precision/recall, and SLO impact estimation (estimated error budget consumed).
- Simulation harness and canary rollout across staging -> canary region -> prod with opt-in teams.

Out of scope for this ticket: deep ML model research for correlation (we will use rule-weighted heuristics + lightweight statistical correlation in this iteration), UI for editing policies (console work will be follow-up), and private deployment packaging (handled in a future dedicated ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Grouped incidents reduce noisy pages by >=60% for historical KV cache burst test across staging logs
No automated remediation executes without: confidence >= 0.85 AND safety whitelist match AND cooldown not active
Pager rate (pages/week) for infra SLO alerts drops by >=50% in the canary region during 2-week trial
All grouped incidents produce a single canonical incident link with links to: runbook, implicated hosts/pools, SLO cost estimate
Dashboards show grouping precision and recall; alerts are traceable back to original signals for postmortems
Playbooks can be executed manually from the incident and be audited in the action log
Rollback: feature can be toggled off globally and per-team within 15 minutes with no residual automation still running

implementation_notes: Use existing Alertmanager webhook to fan-in signals. Build correlation worker as stateless service with short-lived in-memory windows backed by Redis for cross-worker membership consistency.
Policy engine: simple rule weight scoring (signal_type_weight + region_weight + topology_overlap + temporal_decay) -> score in [0,1]. Config per signal family in YAML initially.
Autoremediation adapters: Kubernetes (pod restart, annotate), Node admin (drain/reboot), Routing (soft-fail via smart-router). Each adapter must return action_id and be idempotent.
Audit trail: record original alerts, grouping decision, confidence, executed actions, and SRE override actions to central event store (ELK).
Testing: synthetic storm generator in repo and chaos-runbook to validate safe failover gating. Add integration tests asserting no auto action for confidence < 0.85.
